newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to test An-140 passenger/cargo jet in June.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to test An-140 passenger/cargo jet in June.

text.p: Ukraine's Antonov design bureau will test fly a new An-140 passenger jet next month as part of plans to replace An-24s, the bureau's top designer said on Monday.
"We are just about to complete assembly of the first model An-140. It will have its first test flight near Kiev next month," Antonov's Yuri Skvorchevsky told Reuters.
The short-haul turboprop An-140 is meant to replace the ageing An-24, hundreds of which are being used in the former Soviet Union, Latin America, Africa, Arab countries and China.
The plane will carry 52 passengers and 4.9 tonnes of cargo and will cost $6.5 million -- far less than its Western-made equivalents.
Skvorchevsky put domestic demand at 100 An-140s and demand elsewhere in former Soviet republics at 500 planes by 2005.
The second model of the new An-70 cargo plane was successfully tested with its inaugural flight last month and several flights were scheduled for May.
Kiev has high hopes for the An-70, which is designed for both military and civilian purposes and can carry 35 tonnes of cargo for 3,500 km (2,200 miles).
"Production of An-70s will start next year in Kiev and (the Russian city of) Samara. Market demand is very promising -- at least 2,500 planes in the next few years," Skvorchevsky said.
Experts estimate that two major buyers will be the Russian and Ukrainian defence ministries which have already ordered 500 and 100 of the aircraft respectively.
Antonov blamed human error for the crash of the first prototype, which apparently went out of control and collided with an Antonov plane shadowing it on a test flight near Kiev in February 1995.
